## 2. Contents of package.json (proves an empty/absent dependency manifest)
$ cat package.json
[PASTE OUTPUT HERE — should show "dependencies": {} or no dependencies field at all]

## 3. Confirm no node_modules directory exists
$ ls node_modules 2>&1
[PASTE OUTPUT HERE — should show "No such file or directory" or equivalent]

## 4. Confirm no lockfile exists (no package-lock.json / yarn.lock / pnpm-lock.yaml)
$ ls package-lock.json yarn.lock pnpm-lock.yaml 2>&1
[PASTE OUTPUT HERE — should show "No such file or directory" for all three]

## 5. Grep the source for any require()/import of a third-party package
# (Confirms every import resolves to a Node built-in, not a package.)
$ grep -rn "require(\|from '" src/ | grep -v "node:" | grep -v "^src.*from '\./" | grep -v "^src.*from '\.\./"
[PASTE OUTPUT HERE — should be empty, or only show relative imports between your own files]

## 6. Confirm no shelling out to the `git` binary at runtime
# (Required disclosure per organizer FAQ — this tool reads .git files directly,
# it never invokes an external git process.)
$ grep -rn "child_process\|exec(\|spawn(" src/
[PASTE OUTPUT HERE — should be empty in shipped src/. If any dev-only fixture
generation script uses git, it must live outside src/ and be disclosed in
STDLIB.md, never part of the runtime artifact.]

## 8. Reproducible build — two builds, byte-identical output
$ [BUILD COMMAND] && sha256sum dist/gitxray.js > hash1.txt
$ [BUILD COMMAND] && sha256sum dist/gitxray.js > hash2.txt
$ diff hash1.txt hash2.txt && echo "IDENTICAL"
